 This application coming on for hearing this day, the cou  following:
 ORDER

The applicants have preferred this petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
against the order dated 11.11.2016 passed by the III rd Additional Sessions Judge, Bhopal dismissing the revision petition preferred by the petitioners against the order dated 17.06.2016 passed by the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bhopal in a Criminal Case No. SUM/5770/2015 rejecting the prayer for discharge.
Learned counsel for the applicants contends that M/s Gilbarco Veeder- Root India Pvt. Ltd. is a company registered under the Companies Act, 1956.

Some irregularities were detected during the inspection i.e., the fuel dispensing machines were found to be deficient as the same were not calibrated in accordance with the Legal Mr. Rishi Bhatnagar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70160984/

sentences.text: A complaint was filed against the applicants in their personal capacities and other accused person by the Department of Weights and Measures.
In the complaint so filed by the complainant, the names of the applicants figure at serial no.7 & 8 in the array of accused.

Learned counsel for the applicants, with reference to the contents of the complaint Annexure-A/7 (brought on record as additional document in I.A. No.825), contends that the complaint itself is silent as regard the status and role of the applicants in any capacity what to talk of their status being that of Directors.

Since the Company itself has been arrayed as accused no.10, therefore, the complainant is legally required to show the manner in which the applicants are liable for the omission, if any, done by the Company in not calibrating the fuel dispensing machines in accordance with the Act, 2009.

The applicants have not been shown to be the Directors in the Company and their roles have not been defined as to how they are liable for day to day affairs of the Company in ordinary course of business.
Even the Company has not been impleaded through some responsible person of the Company.
The applicants have been arrayed as accused by names without their being any designation attached to them.

Learned counsel for the applicants, with reference to additional documents on record, submits that the applicant no.1 is not having any designation in the Company nor has the same mentioned in the complaint as to in which capacity, the applicant no.1 has been arrayed as one of the accused.
No role has been ascribed to the applicant as to the day to day affairs of the Company.
The applicant no.2 had already resigned from the Company in the year 2010 and this fact was sought to be brought on record with the help of Form No.32.
The Form No.32 was brought on record in I.A. No.7458, the veracity of which was sought to be verified by the learned counsel for the State on 29.11.2023.
Even thereafter, time was granted to the learned counsel for the State vide order dated 08.01.2024 as well, when last opportunity was sought by the learned counsel for the State to do the needful.
As of now, there is no denial to the Form No.32 issued by the Registrar of the Company.

Even otherwise,
the applicant no.2 has also been impleaded by name without ascribing any specific role to him in the affairs of the Company.

The complaint is conspicuously silent as regards the allegation that the offence was committed with connivance, negligence of the Director, other then the nominated persons who were impleaded as co-accused.

The allegations do not advance the case of the complainant on legal parameters as the complaint does not make out specific allegations with regard to involvement of the applicants by way of connivance, abatement or participation in the affairs of the Company in any manner so as to bring their culpability even on prima-facie basis.
The aforesaid conditions are sine qua non before taking cognizane by the Court in the context of alleged misconduct by the applicants which has not been detailed in any manner in the complaint.

It is relevant to note here that even before filing of the complaint, a specific information was sought by the prosecution on the strength of communication attached as A/5 as to whether the applicants are the Directors of the Company or not.

Even if the information was furnished showing some culpability of the applicants being Directors of the Company, still the prosecution did not implead the applicants as Directors of the Company and did not show any overt act in terms of any responsibility towards day to day affairs of the Company.

The issue is similar to the requirement of law in Negotiable Instruments Act, Fertilizer Control Order, The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 and provision in terms of Section 17(4) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act Mr. Rishi Bhatnagar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70160984/
2 which is pari materia with Section 46 of the Legal Metrology Act.

. Even on the bare perusal of the complaint, taking of cognizance by the Magistrate on the basis of the complaint is nothing but an abuse of process of law and the same is accordingly quashed along with all the subsequent proceedings undertaken in pursuance thereof.
